text: Thursday evening, the drive together into Tavistock
why: Paragraph 13 places the visit on Thursday, the story ends in the evening at Tavistock, and the drive into town follows the visit.

text: Why was the favourite made away with? — nobody meant to carry him off: he was led out to be harmed and got loose
id: q.why_taken=nobody meant to carry him off: he was led out to be harmed and got loose
why: Holmes and the police both discuss the horse bolting or being led out and harmed (¶46, ¶57), so this alternative to a deliberate theft has been raised.

text: Why did Straker go out to the stables at one in the morning? — to do something to the horse himself
id: q.straker_reason=to do something to the horse himself
why: Straker's stated reason for going out is to check on the horses (¶32). Nothing so far suggests he meant to harm the horse himself.

text: Why did Straker have the small knife with him? — to make some fine cut on the horse
id: q.knife=to make some fine cut on the horse
why: The story notes the knife is odd for rough work (¶81) but never suggests a purpose involving a cut on the horse. That specific answer is new.

text: What has lamed three of the sheep in the paddock? — someone cut their legs on purpose, practising for the horse
id: q.sheep_lame=someone cut their legs on purpose, practising for the horse
why: The story reports three lame sheep (¶173) and Holmes's delight, but never suggests deliberate cutting or any practice for the horse.

text: Who lamed the sheep in the paddock?
why: The lad reports the sheep are lame and Holmes shows interest in them, so asking who lamed them is a plain question the story invites.

text: Who lamed the sheep in the paddock? — nobody: it is a natural ailment
id: q.who_lamed_sheep=nobody: it is a natural ailment
why: A natural cause is an obvious alternative to human interference, and the lad's remark that it is 'not of much account' makes it a reasonable possibility to consider.

text: Who lamed the sheep in the paddock? — someone else at King's Pyland
why: The sheep are in the King's Pyland paddock and the story has focused on people at King's Pyland, so a local culprit is a possibility the reader has reason to weigh.
